coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 6–7 miles, Z2 only (140 bpm ceiling), 300–400 ft of rolling vert if available. You're 9 days out and in taper; Wednesday's traditional vert work is *off the table*. Your last three runs averaged 128 bpm—solid, but you're still accruing load. The goal today is blood flow and confidence on terrain without taxing your CNS. If you're traveling for work, a 45-min steady effort on whatever elevation is available will do. Skip any tempo or hill repeats; that window closed two weeks ago.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: You're running on a 6.55-hour sleep night with 77% efficiency—below your 30-day average of 7.63h. This is real sleep debt. Front-load carbohydrate today: 100–120g carbs at breakfast, 30–40g in the 2 hours before your run, and a solid refeed dinner (rice, pasta, or potatoes plus protein). Your resting HR is 60 bpm (lower than your average of 65.4), which is positive, but don't interpret it as permission to under-fuel. Alpine ultras punish glycogen deficits. Hydrate aggressively today—2–3L minimum—to offset any travel dehydration.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Sleep is your rate-limiting factor right now. Tonight, aim for 8+ hours—no negotiation. Taper is when adaptation happens, not during the hard weeks. Your recovery score is 71 (Recovered), which is fine, but the 6.55h of sleep is dragging you backward. Skip the work emails after 9 PM, dial the room temp to 62–65°F if you're in a hotel, and use a sleep app to track trends through race week. Nine days out, one extra hour of sleep matters more than an extra 10 minutes of running.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You've logged 20.6 miles this week versus 35.6 last week—that's the cut you need. Resist the taper panic that tells you to add volume. The Julian Alps 50K will expose poor pacing and weak vertical legs, not lack of base miles. Your work as a Head of Corp Dev means you're managing stress and decision-making all day; bring that discipline to your taper protocol. Nail your nutrition, sleep, and easy runs. The fitness is already in your legs. Race week is about arriving rested and sharp, not second-guessing what you didn't do.
